records.label: Boy with de novo 8q24 deletion

variants.as_reported: de novo deletion on chromosome 8q24 involving the EXT1 gene and additional genes located distal to EXT1

quotes: Here we describe a boy with multiple exostoses, hypertrichosis, mental retardation, and epilepsy due to a de novo deletion on chromosome 8q24.

Molecular analysis revealed that the deletion interval overlaps with the Langer-Giedion syndrome and involves the EXT1 gene and additional genes located distal to EXT1, but probably not encompassing the TRPS1 gene located proximal to EXT1.

records.label: Boy with 8q24 microdeletion

phenotypes.text: fat pads on soles of feet

quotes: We report on a boy with an oligo array-cgh characterized small microdeletion involving EXT1 alone but with some features of Langer-Giedion syndrome suggesting a functional disturbance of TRPS1.

This boy, in addition to a mild Langer-Giedion like phenotype, also had some unusual features including prominent toe pads and fat pads on the soles of his feet similar to those described in Pierpont syndrome.

records.label: Children with RAD21 mutations
quotes: Children with RAD21 mutations display growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlap findings in individuals with CdLS.
Notably, unlike children with mutations in NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3, these individuals have much milder cognitive impairment than those with classical CdLS.
Our data suggest that, compared to loss-of-function mutations, dominant missense mutations result in more severe functional defects and cause worse structural and cognitive clinical findings.

records.label: IV.16
records.segregation: Deletion also found in the mother and two maternal aunts, who did not fulfill CdLS diagnostic criteria
quotes: In a patient with CdLS (IV.16) we identifed a novel single basepair deletion (c.704delG) in RAD21, which encodes a cohesin pathway protein.
Notably, the deletion was found in the mother and the two aunts of the index patient, and none of them had been suspected of having CdLS or a cohesinopathy prior to this study (a).
The index patient can be classified as mild CdLS, but the other family members do not fulfill the diagnostic criteria of CdLS.

records.label: 15-month-old boy
records.segregation: de novo; absent in both healthy parents
quotes: We report a 15-month-old boy presenting with developmental delay, distinct CdLS-like facial features, gastrointestinal reflux in early infancy, testis retention, prominent digit pads and diaphragmatic hernia.
Exome sequencing revealed a novel RAD21 variant, c.1774_1776del, p.(Gln592del), suggestive of CdLS type 4. Segregation analysis of the two healthy parents confirmed the variant as de novo

quotes: A novel RAD21 mutation in a boy with mild Cornelia de Lange presentation: Further delineation of the phenotype.

records.label: Patient with holoprosencephaly
quotes: Another case of holoprosencephaly associated with RAD21 loss-of-function variant.

notes.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations (24 intragenic variants, 7 microdeletions), 24 previously unpublished. In the 29 with full clinical information, the phenotype was an attenuated CdLS phenotype compared with that caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, particularly for facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition, and behavior.
quotes: We gathered a series of 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations [24 different intragenic sequence variants (2 recurrent), 7 unique microdeletions], including 24 hitherto unpublished cases.
Their phenotype is an attenuated CdLS phenotype compared to that caused by variants in NIPBL or SMC1A for facial morphology, limb anomalies, and especially for cognition and behavior.

notes.statement: In the 29 patients with sufficient data (cohort A), Krab et al. (2020) found postnatal microcephaly in 16/28, postnatal short stature in 10/27, synophrys in 19/28, long and/or smooth philtrum in 26/29, short fifth finger in 23/28, cleft palate in 6/25, heart anomalies in 9/23, hearing loss in 8/24, and gastroesophageal reflux in 13/25; no major limb malformations were found (0/29).
quotes: Postnatal head circumference < − 2SD | HP:0000252 | 16/28 | 57
Major limb malformation | HP:0001180/HP:0009776 | 0/29 | 0
Hearing loss | HP:0000365 | 8/24 | 33

notes.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found that most RAD21 patients (16/29, 55%) had normal or mildly impaired cognition, all patients aged 3 years and above used some words, and 14/25 had behavioral problems, mainly anxiety, ADHD, ASD and obsessive-compulsive behavior; aggression and self-injurious behavior were uncommon (each 1 patient).
quotes: The majority of RAD21 patients (16/29, 55%) have normal or mildly impaired cognitive functioning (SMC1A group 32%; NIPBL group 7%)
14/25 RAD21 patients (56%) with sufficiently available information on behavior had problems, mainly features of anxiety, ADHD, ASD, and obsessive–compulsive behavior.

notes.statement: Krab et al. (2020) noted unusual anomalies in RAD21 cases including vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and relatively frequent malformations of foregut-derived structures; short stature and microcephaly typically developed postnatally.
quotes: Unusual anomalies in the RAD21 cases are vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae).
Malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut are relatively frequent in RAD21 patients and have only rarely been described in CdLS
Patients with RAD21 variants have generally less impaired growth at birth, and short stature and microcephaly develop postnatally.

notes.statement: Krab et al. (2020) suggested that biallelic RAD21 variants can cause Mungan syndrome and monoallelic variants can cause holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics; involvement of RAD21 variants in sclerocornea and schizophrenia was uncertain.
quotes: The (limited) available information of individuals from cohort B suggests that biallelic RAD21 variants can also lead to Mungan syndrome and monoallelic RAD21 variants to holoprosencephaly (like one case in cohort A) and possibly schizophrenia, although in the latter the association may be a spurious coincidence.

notes.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found that variants were frequently familial (9 of 21 index cases in whom inheritance could be established), with 13 of 24 sequence variants predicted truncating and scattered throughout the gene, while missense variants tended to cluster at protein-binding domains. Six of the seven deletions included other genes in addition to RAD21.
quotes: A relatively large proportion of the cases are familial (nine out of 21 index cases for whom inheritance could be established). The seven CNVs were all deletions, six of which included other genes in addition to RAD21.
The missense variants tend to cluster at the functional domains of the protein.

notes.statement: By protein modeling and molecular dynamics of 12 RAD21 variants, Krab et al. (2020) predicted that Ser345Pro impairs and Pro376Arg over-stabilizes the RAD21-STAG2 interaction, Cys585Arg and Arg586Gln destabilize the RAD21-SMC1A domain, and Gln592del and Leu603Pro displace Lys605 affecting SMC1A ATPase site 1; Arg65Gln, Phe600del, Ser618Gly and Ala622Thr caused no structural alteration.
quotes: The structural and functional analysis indicated that at least six out of twelve modeled RAD21 missense variants are likely pathogenic (Ser345Pro, Pro367Arg, Cys585Arg, Arg586Gln (reported as a VUS), Gln592del and Leu603Pro).
The Cys585Arg and Arg586Gln variants destabilize the RAD21-SMC1A domain; and Gln592del and Leu603Pro (but not Phe600del) disturb the cyclic process through the dislocation of Lys605.

notes.statement: Krab et al. (2020) observed a trend toward higher CdLS scores and more impaired growth in patients with microdeletions than intragenic variants, but no difference between truncating and nontruncating variants; striking interfamilial and intrafamilial variability, especially in cognition and behavior, was not explained by mosaicism in most families.
quotes: There was a trend towards higher CdLS scores and more frequently impaired growth parameters in patients with microdeletions compared to those with intragenic variants, but no differences were apparent in frequency of major malformations or cognitive and behavioral problems.
The intrafamilial variation cannot be explained by mosaicism in most families.

notes.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found that all cohort A patients had CdLS scores of at least 5 and no RAD21 variant would have been missed using the CdLS consensus criteria for molecular testing; CdLS was suspected before testing in about 60% of index cases.
quotes: No RAD21 variant would have been missed using the CdLS consensus criteria for molecular studies (Kline et al. 2018).
In about 60% of index cases (13/21 index cases in which this was specified) CdLS was suspected prior to testing.

notes.statement: Krab et al. (2020) recommended parental testing even when parents appear unaffected, periodic formal neuropsychological and behavioral screening, and, for a RAD21 VUS of undetermined pathogenicity, testing of other CdLS genes or exome/genome sequencing.
quotes: Parental testing is warranted, even if signs or symptoms are apparently absent in parents, and standard testing of parents may further broaden the phenotype of RAD21 variants.
Periodic formal screening for neuropsychological and behavioral problems is still warranted in all individuals with RAD21 variants

notes.statement: Kruszka et al. (2019) found that knocking down STAG2 and SMC1A with shRNA in human neural stem cells changed the expression of the holoprosencephaly-associated genes ZIC2, GLI2, SMAD3 and FGFR1. They concluded that the cohesin complex is an important regulator of median forebrain development.
quotes: we found that shRNA knockdown of STAG2 and SMC1A causes aberrant expression of HPE-associated genes ZIC2, GLI2, SMAD3 and FGFR1 in human neural stem cells
These findings show the cohesin complex as an important regulator of median forebrain development

notes.statement: Using whole-mount in situ hybridization in mouse embryos, Kruszka et al. (2019) found that Stag2 and Smc1a are expressed in the prosencephalic neural folds during primary neurulation. This expression pattern fits a role in forebrain morphogenesis.
quotes: Using whole mount in situ hybridization, we show that STAG2 and SMC1A are expressed in the prosencephalic neural folds during primary neurulation in the mouse, consistent with forebrain morphogenesis and holoprosencephaly pathogenesis.

notes.statement: Dorval et al. (2020) noted that, among the genes causing Cornelia de Lange syndrome, RAD21 is associated with a milder phenotype, and that very few RAD21 intragenic mutations had been identified.
quotes: Among them, RAD21 is associated with a milder phenotype. Very few RAD21 intragenic mutations have been identified so far.

notes.statement: Gudmundsson et al. (2019) used in silico structural modeling to predict that the RAD21 p.Gln592del variant disrupts contact between RAD21 Lys591 and SMC1A residues Glu1191 and Glu1192, altering the RAD21-SMC1A interface.
quotes: Assessment by in silico structural model predicted that the p.Gln592del variant results in a discontinued contact between RAD21-Lys591 and the SMC1A residues Glu1191 and Glu1192, causing changes in the RAD21-SMC1A interface.

notes.statement: Boyle et al. (2017) found the RAD21 c.704delG variant in a patient with mild CdLS and in his or her mother and two aunts, none of whom fulfilled diagnostic criteria for CdLS. They suggested that RAD21 variants are associated with incomplete penetrance and that such individuals may be underdiagnosed.
quotes: The index patient can be classified as mild CdLS, but the other family members do not fulfill the diagnostic criteria of CdLS.
This study together with previous reports suggests incomplete penetrance associated with RAD21 variants and these individuals may therefore be underdiagnosed.

notes.statement: Minor et al. (2014) reported the first intragenic deletion and frameshift mutations in RAD21 in patients with atypical CdLS. The patient with the in-frame exon 13 deletion was more mildly affected than the patient with the frameshift mutation. The authors discussed variable clinical presentation within families and low penetrance of the mutations.
quotes: We report the first intragenic deletion and frameshift mutations identified in RAD21 in two patients presenting with atypical CdLS.

Moreover, the variability of clinical presentation within families and low penetrance of mutations as well as the significance of performing molecular genetic testing in mildly affected patients are discussed.

notes.statement: Minor et al. (2014) stressed the clinical value of RAD21 mutation analysis in patients with atypical forms of CdLS.
quotes: This study expands the spectrum of RAD21 mutations and emphasizes the clinical utility of performing RAD21 mutation analysis in patients presenting with atypical forms of CdLS.

notes.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) found that the RAD21 mutations acted at the interface between RAD21 and the other cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A, and that they impaired the cellular DNA damage response.
quotes: Mechanistically, these mutations act at the RAD21 interface with the other cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A, impair cellular DNA damage response, and disrupt transcription in a zebrafish model.

notes.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) showed that the RAD21 mutations disrupted transcription in a zebrafish model.
quotes: Mechanistically, these mutations act at the RAD21 interface with the other cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A, impair cellular DNA damage response, and disrupt transcription in a zebrafish model.

notes.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) suggested that dominant missense mutations in RAD21 caused more severe functional defects than loss-of-function mutations, along with worse structural and cognitive clinical findings.
quotes: Our data suggest that, compared to loss-of-function mutations, dominant missense mutations result in more severe functional defects and cause worse structural and cognitive clinical findings.

notes.statement: Wuyts et al. (2002) described a boy with multiple exostoses, hypertrichosis, mental retardation, and epilepsy who had a de novo submicroscopic interstitial deletion at 8q24. The deletion overlapped the Langer-Giedion syndrome region and included EXT1 and additional genes distal to EXT1, but it probably did not include TRPS1, which lies proximal to EXT1.
quotes: Molecular analysis revealed that the deletion interval overlaps with the Langer-Giedion syndrome and involves the EXT1 gene and additional genes located distal to EXT1, but probably not encompassing the TRPS1 gene located proximal to EXT1.
